subject: URGENT: Production latency surge and token errors — suspected HOL blocking in KV cache
messages:

Cc: support@stellarnet.com
Date: 2027-04-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spike and 502/504 errors — urgent

Hi Olga —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency (~3.2s -> 12s) and intermittent 502/504s across our inference routes around 07:50 PDT this morning. Throughput dropped by ~40% and a non-trivial number of requests returned tokenization/kv-access errors.

Attached is a small sample of traces and a consumer-side log. Key observations:
- Spikes match a burst of similar prompts (many share a common long prefix).
- The error payload often mentions KV cache misses and timeouts.
- The issue affects both dev and prod clusters in us-west and us-east.

This is customer-facing traffic; it’s impacting our session freshness and we are getting escalation from our CTO. Please advise immediate mitigation (we can throttle or divert traffic on our side, but need your guidance).

Attachments: logs_2027-04-18.zip

Thanks,
Priyanka

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike and 502/504 errors — urgent

Quick technical triage (initial findings):

- Root suspicion: head-of-line (HOL) blocking in KV cache caused by an interaction between the new "hot-prefix" caching policy and the recent batch-lane selector change we rolled last week.
  - The hot-prefix policy pins prefixes into a shared KV hotset; under bursty, similar-prefix workloads this led to KV backend lock contention and long wait times for cache population.
  - The batch-lane selector was inadvertently sending large coherent groups of long-prefix requests into the same batch lane; this created long tail serialization inside the batch executor.

- Evidence:
  - Increased KV backend queue depth visible in the trace events attached to the logs you sent.
  - Correlated spikes when many requests shared the same initial 64 tokens.
  - Error reports show timeouts coming from the cache-populate RPC on the GPU host.

Immediate mitigations we can apply now (risk/ETA):
1) Disable hot-prefix pinning on the affected model pool (low risk, 5-8min to flip).
2) Reduce per-lane max batch size from 48 -> 16 and shorten lane timeouts (low-medium risk, 3-10min).
3) If the previous two don’t restore baseline, route 20% of traffic to quantized model variant q3-mini for the route to reduce GPU occupancy (medium risk, 15-25min including canary).

I’m attaching a small patch (kv-config-diff.patch) with the config changes. I recommend 1+2 immediate, and we can perform 3 if p99 remains >2s after mitigations.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-mitigation summary and next steps — Stellarnet incident (resolved)

Team / Priyanka / Alex —

Summary (what we did):
- 2027-04-18 10:15 PDT: Disabled hot-prefix pinning on the affected pool and reduced per-lane batch size from 48 -> 16.
- 2027-04-18 10:22 PDT: Observed immediate p99 improvement from ~11.3s -> 1.8s and error rate fell to baseline. Throughput recovered to ~95% of pre-incident levels within 12 minutes.
- We ran a 20% fallback to q3-mini for 30 minutes as a canary; that helped reduce backend GPU pressure during the drain.

Root cause (short): HOL blocking in the KV cache under high-coherence prefix bursts. Two changes combined badly: the hot-prefix pinning increased lock contention for cache population, and the batch-lane selector grouped similar long-prefix requests into the same executor lane, creating long-tail serialization.

Actions and follow-ups:
1) Short-term (completed): the two mitigations above.
2) Near-term (engineering): add adaptive hotset eviction heuristics, add safeguards to batch-lane selector to detect high-prefix-coherence and split lanes earlier. (Vivek to own).
3) Postmortem write-up and exec briefing: I’ll produce the technical timeline and attach traces + kv-config-diff for review. Target: draft by 2027-04-23.
4) Commercial: Markus + Stephanie to propose service credit; Monica to coordinate the exec call with Stellarnet.

Metrics: restored p99 < 2s, error rate down to baseline, throughput >=95% — see dashboard: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4821

Attachments: kv-config-diff.patch, bridge-incident-screenshot.png

Thanks everyone for quick coordination. I’ll schedule the postmortem review for next week and invite the customer.
